Definition: from G303 and G4717; to recrucify (figuratively):--crucify afresh.
BiblicalUsage: The word appears once: if they shall fall away, it is impossible to renew them again unto repentance, seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put Him to an open shame. It is crucifying again — not a second cross on Calvary, but the apostate's fresh rejection, treating the Son of God as though His crucifixion were not finished.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for crucifying afresh carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the warning — to fall away after tasting the heavenly gift is to crucify the Son of God again, and put Him to open shame.
